title: PR-level traffic replay with adaptive quantile anchoring
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Prevent noisy or spurious CI PR failures while catching meaningful latency/regression signals by replaying representative multi-workload traffic against a PR commit in an isolated CI runner and comparing anchored quantiles against a canonical baseline branch. The harness composes short microburst, steady-state, and embeddings-heavy workloads; warms KV cache where appropriate; and applies an adaptive quantile anchoring technique to make p95/p99 comparisons robust to distributional shifts introduced by small PR changes.

Why this ticket: Existing CI gating captures throughput regressions but still has high false-positive rates on p95 when workloads shift slightly or KV warming differs. We need a reproducible replay + statistical decision rule that reduces noise while retaining sensitivity to real regressions important for customer-facing SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: PRs run the replay harness as part of the perf pipeline and produce a standardized report artifact (JSON + HTML) linked in the PR
Gating rule: a PR is flagged only if the posterior probability of an increase in anchored p95 > 10% is >= 0.95 AND the effect is observed on at least two independent workload slices

Baseline anchoring: for every PR run, the harness computes anchored quantiles using the last 10 canonical branch runs; baseline stability check must pass (coefficient of variation < 8%) or the run is marked 'baseline-unstable' and results are advisory

End-to-end run time for a standard PR (3 workload slices) must be <= 25 minutes on CI runner hardware (with pre-warm step), or the harness falls back to a lightweight fast-scan mode for quick feedback
False positive rate measured on historical PR corpus must be < 1% across the last 200 test PRs after tuning
implementation_plan: Spike: implement replay composer that can synthesize three slice types (microburst, steady-state, embeddings-heavy) from trace inputs (done)
Instrument: add token-level timers and KV-warm hooks into the CI runner agent to capture warm/cold variations
Anchoring: implement quantile-anchoring library that uses order-statistic smoothing + Bayesian posterior for p95/p99 deltas
CI integration: add a pipeline step that spins an isolated perf runner, executes baseline then PR commit, uploads result artifact to artifacts store
Decision rule: implement gating lambda that consumes artifact and posts status back to PR; include hysteresis to avoid flapping
Dashboards & alerts: Grafana board for slice-level quantiles, and an alert if baseline stability drops or false-positive triggers spike
Rollout: start in advisory mode for two weeks, evaluate FP/FN, then flip to enforced gating
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KV cache warming differences between baseline and PR cause spurious regressions. Mitigation: include explicit warm-up step and report warm/cold-separated quantiles
Risk: Long CI runtime increases PR turnaround. Mitigation: fast-scan mode to give early advisory signal; enforce heavier check only on release branches or large diff PRs
Risk: Overfitting decision thresholds to historical dataset. Mitigation: cross-validate on held-out PR sets and measure FPR/FNR before enforcement
Risk: Workload composition mismatch with real production. Mitigation: periodically update slice weights from traffic telemetry (weekly) and surface change logs in the artifact

2026-03-08: First CI runs showed high variance on embeddings-heavy slice; adjusted synthetic inter-arrival distribution and increased warm-up to 60s. New runs show reduced variance (CoV down from 15% to 6%).
